evals.prompt: Build a tiny Bun CLI that uses @k2b/nessi/ai with OpenRouter to summarize text passed as a command-line argument. It should print streamed text as it arrives and read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the environment.
evals.expected_output: A concise Bun/TypeScript CLI using openAICompatible() with an OpenRouter base URL, provider.stream(), block_start/block_delta text handling, issue/usage event handling, and no browser-exposed secrets.

evals.prompt: I want a provider switcher for my Node service: use local Ollama in development and OpenAI in production. Show the @k2b/nessi/ai code and keep the rest of the app independent from the provider choice.
evals.expected_output: A provider factory returning the shared Provider interface, using openAICompatible() with per-endpoint compat settings (for example a local Ollama /v1 endpoint and OpenAI), plus an example complete() call.

evals.prompt: Show me how to do tool calling with @k2b/nessi/ai only. I have a search_docs function and want the model to request it, then send the tool result back for a final answer.
evals.expected_output: A consumer-side tool-call loop using tools inputSchema, complete(), assistant tool_call block extraction, tool_result messages, and a follow-up complete() call. It should mention that @k2b/nessi/ai does not execute tools automatically.

evals.prompt: Build a tiny Bun agent with @k2b/nessi that stores history in memory, uses OpenRouter, defines one server-side search_docs tool with zod, and streams text to stdout.
evals.expected_output: A concise agent-loop example importing nessi, defineTool, and memoryStore from @k2b/nessi, importing openAICompatible from @k2b/nessi/ai, defining a zod-backed server tool, passing store: memoryStore() and tools to nessi(), and iterating loop events for block_start/block_delta text handling, issue handling, and loop_end.aggregate/loopId handling.

evals.prompt: I need a typed task extractor with @k2b/nessi. It should return a validated Zod object and accept an image input.
evals.expected_output: A root nessi.structured() example importing nessi from @k2b/nessi, importing a provider from @k2b/nessi/ai, defining a Zod output schema, passing string or multimodal content parts as input, passing no tools (structured() takes none; tool work belongs in nessi()), and reading result.output plus result.structuredMeta/result.aggregate. It should not use complete(provider, request) for the high-level typed task unless explicitly discussing low-level responseFormat.

evals.prompt: My Nessi loop runs in a background worker, but steering instructions arrive through separate HTTP requests and are stored in my database. Show how the worker can pick them up without continuously polling while the provider or tools are running. I also need local loop.steer() to keep working and want to show applied steering in the UI.
evals.expected_output: A root nessi() example using the optional steering callback to return one pending message, an ordered array, or undefined from application-owned persistence, while retaining loop.steer(). It should handle steer_applied as the shared UI confirmation, explain that Nessi checks only at safe loop boundaries including before provider calls and normal completion, and leave claiming, persistence, and delivery guarantees to the application.

evals.prompt: My shell tool returns very large output. I need the full output during the current Nessi loop and in storage/UI, but later user requests should send only exit code, changed files, and a short excerpt to the model. Show the supported API and explain resume behavior.
evals.expected_output: A root defineTool() example using optional toHistoricalResult({ input, output, callId }). It should explain that Nessi derives and persists the historical value once, same-loop provider calls and resumes with the same loopId use the full result, later loop IDs use the historical value, storage/events/aggregates retain the full result, failures emit non-fatal tool_historical_result_error, and maxToolResultChars applies afterward.
